# Choose membership and network resources

SpaMTP uses [RaMP-DB](https://github.com/ncats/RaMP-DB) for identifiers and
pathway memberships, and [graphite](https://bioconductor.org/packages/graphite/)
for archived topology. Memberships define enrichment and score calculations;
network edges supply interaction context for displaying those results.

| Resource | Contents and use |
|:--|:--|
| `source_df`, `analyte` | Resolve measured identifiers to RaMP entities |
| `pathway`, `analytehaspathway` | Build pathway memberships and measured universes |
| `chem_props` | Chemical properties for mass-based annotation |
| `ramp_kegg` | Human Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) interactions |
| `ramp_reactome` | Human Reactome interactions |
| `ramp_wikipathway` | Human WikiPathways interactions |
| `ramp_hmdb` | Human Small Molecule Pathway Database (SMPDB) interactions, under the historical SpaMTP resource name |

Load only the required collections. The [joint-pathway guide](Gene_Identifier_Mapping.html#joint-ms-and-rna-pathways)
uses memberships for measured genes and metabolites. The
[annotation guide](Metabolite_Annotation_Pipeline.html#carry-the-annotation-threshold-into-real-pathway-analysis)
shows how scored compound identities enter a network.

## Snapshot versions and interpretation

RaMP 3.0.7 memberships and graphite archive-19 topology (2022-11-01) have separate
provenance. Source-specific pathway IDs and memberships are retained during
identifier reconciliation. A pathway can have substantial measured membership
and sparse available topology. Inspect both before interpreting a network.
The network page generated by `pathwayNetworkPlots()` selects pathways by name;
filter to one database when names recur across sources.

# Inspect a pathway and its interactions

`db` holds the requested collection. `cell_cycle$protEdges` records protein
interactions, including source labels and direction. The example uses the pinned
KEGG Cell Cycle pathway `hsa:04110` to inspect the available network evidence.

```{r load-graphs, message=FALSE}
library(SpaMTP)
db <- loadSpaMTPDatabase("ramp_kegg", version = "3.0.7")
cell_cycle <- db$ramp_kegg[["Cell cycle"]]
edges <- cell_cycle$protEdges
edge_types <- as.data.frame(table(edges$source_reaction_type),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
colnames(edge_types) <- c("source_label", "interaction_rows")
edge_types <- edge_types[order(-edge_types$interaction_rows), ]
knitr::kable(head(edges[, c("src", "dest", "directed", "source_reaction_type")]),
    row.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(nrow(edges) == 1009L, nrow(edge_types) == 11L)
```

The `r format(nrow(edges), big.mark = ",")` rows describe recorded interactions; repeated endpoint pairs
can have distinct labels or directions. Generic processes retain their source
labels, and undirected edges have no arrowhead. These records support biological
context; causal conclusions require experimental evidence.

## Interaction coverage

Figure 6.\@ref(fig:interaction-types) shows the frequency of archived interaction
types. Counts describe database records for this pathway.

```{r interaction-types, crop=NULL, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.5, out.width="640px", fig.cap="Interaction types in the pinned KEGG Cell Cycle graph. Each bar counts protein-edge records with the indicated source label; endpoint pairs may occur in more than one interaction type. The graph contains 1,009 edge records across 11 types."}
ggplot2::ggplot(edge_types, ggplot2::aes(
    x = reorder(source_label, interaction_rows), y = interaction_rows)) +
    ggplot2::geom_col(fill = "#1a81c2", width = 0.7) +
    ggplot2::coord_flip() +
    ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(6, 16, 6, 6)) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = "Recorded protein interactions")
```

# Inspect resource provenance

The original graph conversion reused the first edge's interaction and direction
codes across each table, losing per-edge labels and merging distinct parallel
interactions. The loader restores these fields from the archived source.
`spamtp_database` identifies the loaded source and checksum;
`spamtp_interaction_repair` records the correction applied in memory.
Corrections apply to exact fingerprint matches of the pinned snapshot.
Save the returned collection with `saveRDS()` to retain both.

```{r inspect-provenance}
attr(db$ramp_kegg, "spamtp_database")
attr(db$ramp_kegg, "spamtp_interaction_repair")
provenance_file <- system.file("extdata", "pathway_interactions_provenance.csv",
                              package = "SpaMTP")
audit_file <- system.file("extdata", "pathway_interactions_audit.csv",
                         package = "SpaMTP")
stopifnot(file.exists(provenance_file), file.exists(audit_file))
knitr::kable(utils::read.csv(audit_file), row.names = FALSE)
```

The audit summarizes all four collections. `edges_after` exceeds `edges_before`
because the correction restores parallel edges that the original conversion
merged. Published files retain their original checksums; SpaMTP records
corrections separately when loading verified snapshots. These edge corrections
leave RaMP memberships and membership-based enrichment unchanged.

## Maintainer recipe

<details>
<summary>Rebuild the pinned interaction correction from a source checkout</summary>

The [source-checkout recipe](https://github.com/SpaMTP-project/SpaMTP/blob/main/data-raw/rebuild_pathway_interactions.R)
uses the identifier and interaction helpers in the same `data-raw` directory.
These development scripts operate on a source checkout. Installed-package users
can inspect the input URLs and checksums in `provenance_file` above.

Download the graphite archive-19 files and original RaMP source mapping listed
in that CSV, stage the pinned SpaMTPdb 3.0.7 resources, then run from the checkout:

```sh
Rscript data-raw/rebuild_pathway_interactions.R \
  /path/to/graphite-19 /path/to/initial-source_df.rda \
  /path/to/SpaMTPdb-resources/3.0.7
```

The recipe checks input fingerprints and reconstructs archived mappings before
restoring source interaction labels. New resource releases require new
fingerprints and provenance records.

</details>
